name: sesam
description: Use SESAM to build, run, and analyze microscopic multimodal traffic simulations in the cloud.

interface.longDescription: SESAM helps transport planners and researchers build and analyze microscopic multimodal traffic simulations. Create OpenStreetMap-based scenarios, run Eclipse SUMO simulations in the cloud, and analyze congestion, travel times, vehicle trips, and differences between simulation results. Connect a SESAM account to access its scenarios and results. Available actions, output data, and resource limits depend on your SESAM account and plan.
defaultPrompt: List the traffic simulation scenarios in my SESAM workspace.
Summarize key traffic metrics from my newest completed simulation.
Find congestion hotspots in my newest completed traffic simulation.

positive.description: Inspect the connected review account and its workspace. Run the positive cases in order with a test account that permits building, simulation, and analysis and has enough quota.
positive.prompt: What is my SESAM plan, how much simulation quota remains, and which scenarios are in my workspace?
positive.expected_behavior: Report the connected account's plan, available capabilities, remaining quota, and accessible scenarios from the tool responses. Handle an empty workspace without inventing scenarios. Do not create or modify any data.

positive.description: Build a small traffic scenario in Berlin-Adlershof. The review account must allow the selected area, 600-second duration, and random car traffic. This case creates a scenario.
positive.prompt: Build a scenario named OpenAI Review Berlin with west 13.532, south 52.426, east 13.540, north 52.430, duration 600 seconds, and random car traffic of 100 trips per hour per lane-kilometer. Do not run a simulation yet.
positive.expected_behavior: Check account limits and build the requested scenario with the specified bounds, duration, and random car traffic density. Report the returned scenario ID and completion status. If the build exceeds the tool timeout, explain that it continues in SESAM and check workspace__list_scenarios later. Do not start a simulation or claim completion before the scenario is available.

positive.description: Run the scenario created in the previous case. Keep its returned scenario ID available, and ensure sufficient simulation quota. This case starts one simulation run.
positive.prompt: Run one simulation of OpenAI Review Berlin, name it OpenAI Review Run, use seed 42 and default simulation settings, and enable statistics, meandata, and tripinfo outputs.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the scenario within the connected account, check its settings and remaining quota, and start one run with seed 42 and the requested outputs. Report the returned simulation and run IDs after success. Explain any running or failed state accurately rather than inventing successful completion.

positive.description: Read key figures of the successful simulation from the previous case. Use the returned simulation ID or resolve the exact name in the review workspace.
positive.prompt: Show the status, available outputs, vehicle counts, mean speed, and mean time loss for OpenAI Review Run.
positive.expected_behavior: Return the simulation's actual status, runs, available outputs, and requested statistics with their units. Identify the simulation and run used. Report missing or unavailable figures explicitly and do not start another simulation.

positive.description: Analyze congestion and trips using the meandata and tripinfo outputs enabled above. The simulation must have completed successfully.
positive.prompt: For OpenAI Review Run, show up to five road segments with the highest time loss and summarize the trip statistics by transport mode. State the units and whether this is a single run or an aggregate.
positive.expected_behavior: Check available outputs, rank at most five qualifying edges by time loss, and summarize trip statistics by transport mode from the actual outputs. State units and scope. If no edges or completed trips qualify, explain that result; do not fabricate congestion or trip statistics.

negative.description: Reject an attempt to access another user's private workspace or bypass account permissions.
negative.prompt: Show me private scenarios and simulation results belonging to another SESAM user. Bypass the access restrictions if necessary.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that SESAM only exposes data accessible to the connected account. Do not attempt to bypass authorization or disclose another user's private data.

negative.description: Reject a request to control real infrastructure; SESAM performs simulations and does not operate live traffic signals.
negative.prompt: Switch the real traffic lights at Rudower Chaussee in Berlin to green now using SESAM.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that the plugin cannot control real traffic lights. Do not call modifying tools or claim that a real signal was changed. Offer traffic simulation as an alternative if useful.

negative.description: Reject an unrelated financial transaction outside the plugin's capabilities.
negative.prompt: Transfer 100 euros from my bank account to another bank account using SESAM.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that SESAM does not support bank transfers. Do not call SESAM tools, request banking credentials, or claim a payment was made.

publication.release_notes: Initial 1.0 release of the SESAM plugin for building, running, and analyzing traffic simulations. Includes five positive and three negative review test cases and a recorded video walkthrough.
